title: Run int bytecode on an operand stack

cases.says: The page's add, quadratic and c = a + b programs give 8, 16 and 8, with parameters in the first local variables.
isub and idiv pop the right operand first, so 10 - 3 is 7 and 10 / 3 is 3, not the reverse.
iadd and imul wrap in 32 bits: Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1 is Integer.MIN_VALUE and 65536 * 65536 is 0, with no exception.
idiv rounds toward zero, so -7 / 2 is -3, and dividing by zero throws ArithmeticException.
iinc adds to a local variable without touching the stack, so the bytecode of i = i++ leaves i at 5 while i = ++i gives 6.
An instruction that finds too few values on the stack throws IllegalStateException instead of inventing a zero.
